lines.text: Morning.
Mind the cart.
Two coppers for a turnip. Two!
Bread's up again. It's always up.
Rain by evening, my knee says.
You're not from the Waystation.
Another one off the road. They keep coming.
Don't stand in the well-queue unless you're drawing.
Is that blood? Don't tell me.
Chid rang the bell twice this morning. Nobody's told him once does it.
The Flagon's ale is half water. The water's half ale.
Evening. Get indoors soon.
Nothing good walks about after dark.
Lamps are lit. Stay where they reach.
Is that the watch? Oh. You.
Shit weather, shit road, shit luck. Morning.
Bloody wolves. Bloody Watch. Bloody bread.
Holloway couldn't find his own arse with a lantern and a map.
Pell counts his coin in bed. Alone, obviously.
If the wolves don't get you, Rook's stew will.
My husband went out to the Verge a month back. Some days I hope he stays out.
Sella took three coppers off me for a smile. Worth four.
Rook's upstairs rooms go by the hour now. Don't ask how I know.
Somebody's having a better night than me. Rook's walls are thin.
Buried two this week. The ground's full and the priest's a fool. Says so himself.
They buried Aldo this morning. The Captain carried the front of the coffin himself.
Keep walking, hero. I've had my fill of heroes.
You smell like the dead. No offence. Everybody does, lately.
Came up the Low Ford at night? You're brave or daft.
They say the Ford-Warden's down. Was that you?
My gran swore the Warden was a story to keep children off the ford.
Wolves took the Oswin goats. In daylight!
Holloway's paying five a pelt, if you've the stomach.
Wolves don't behave like that. Not healthy ones.
Wolves at the gate last night. At the gate!
Tam's farm was hit. Poor lad's sleeping in the Watch-house.
You're the one who cleared the wolves. My boy can walk to the mill again.
Quiet out east now. Too quiet, Maeca says.
They say wolves walk beside you out there. I'd not believe it but for Maeca's face.
Wolf-friend. Keep them out of my hen-house, that's all I ask.
Tam says the stream runs clear again. Tam says a lot, but still.
Wenna's been smiling. Wenna. Smiling.
Pell's diggers moved their pipe. Pell Varrow, doing a kindness. Check your purse.
Heard somebody sold the Dig to Pell. Heard it was you.
You lied to Holloway about the wolves. Everybody knows. He does too.
Harlan's not slept since the wagons went.
The Coyle wagons had the Oswin girl's wedding cloth on them.
Kerchiefs, they say. Red rags and no mercy.
Jory Coyle's home! Harlan wept in the street, I saw it.
Those poor teamsters. Harlan hasn't opened the shutters.
Pell Varrow, selling his own neighbours. I bought eggs from that man.
Pell's been generous lately. With you, especially.
Kerchiefs hit the Penhale farm again. Prices'll climb, you watch.
Salt's doubled. The Kerchiefs are bleeding the road dry.
The Roost burned, they say. You could see the smoke from the wall.
Redcowl dead. I'll believe it when I see the hat.
You made a deal with Redcowl? With Redcowl?
That's Coyle cloth on your back, isn't it.
Harlan says you brought every crate home. Every one.
Wanted, they said at the Watch. Wanted! You've a nerve walking here.
Did you feel the ground go, last night? Like something rolling over.
The shrine lamp's lit. First time since I was a girl.
Vonnra read your fortune? She never reads for free.
Chid says you died. You look well on it.
They carried you in past my door. I thought that was you done.
Are you a knight?
Tag! You're it!
Mum says not to talk to you.
Show us your sword! Go on!
Did you kill a wolf? A big one?
Is it true you've got a wolf for a friend?
All quiet. Keep it that way.
Gates are shut till dawn.
Walk on, traveller.
Piss off home. It's past curfew.
Keep that blade sheathed or I'll sheathe it for you.
Captain's doubled the gate. Wolves.
Pack tore Tam's farm to bits. His Pa was in town, thank God. Somebody fetched him in.
Chid's not aged a day since my mam was a girl. Says it's clean living. Have you SEEN where he lives?
That's the one. Don't look. DON'T look.
They say that one's killed more than the fever year did.
Captain says to let you be. Captain says it like he's not sure.
Is that a woman in all that? Good for her. Good for her.
Are you a lady knight? Are there lady knights?
Don't stand so near the thatch, spark-hands.
Evening. Please don't hit me. Evening.
They say you could hear them from the ridge. The ones in the cages. They say it went on a while.
Harlan stood at the graves the whole afternoon. Didn't say a word. Didn't take his hat off, either. Forgot he had it on.
You can still see their lamps up on the hill at night. Fewer every night.
Sella's got a new customer, the walls are saying. The walls are very specific.
The Flagon's piss is cheaper than the Flagon's ale, and honestly? You can't tell.
My wife ran off with a tinker. Best thing that ever happened to the tinker.
Kerchief lad tried his luck with my daughter. She broke his nose with a bucket. Never been prouder.
If you're going to throw up, do it in the trough. The horses have seen worse.
Indoors, before I find a reason. I'm good at finding reasons.
Sella was singing on the stairs this morning. Sella. Singing. Somebody's in trouble.
Brannoc's girl went south with Wat's cart a fortnight back. Quietest forge in the valley since, and that's saying something.
They buried Brannoc's girl behind the shrine this morning. Chid sang. Chid can't sing. Nobody minded.
Brannoc's stopping carters off the south road, asking after a red-haired girl. Nobody's had the heart to say they've not seen her.
Jessop from the toll owes me four coppers and a ladder. Gone south, they say. Took neither.
Penhales' dog won't go in the barn. Stands at the door and whines at the floor.
A Kerchief bought a sack of oats at the market and PAID for it. In coin. My husband says it's the end of the world.
Watch brought old Corran home from the ford post. Wrote him down a deserter, they did. Deserted to where, I ask you.
Jory Coyle's stopped calling his uncle Uncle. Calls him Mister Coyle in the shop, in front of customers.
They say a cart went out of the east gate the night Pell vanished, and Vonnra let it through without the toll. Vonnra. Without the toll.
Pell Varrow's gone south on a horse he hadn't paid for. Course he hadn't.
Captain's had a letter with a silver seal. Hasn't said a word since. Not that he says many.
